ui.lunarSecret.title: The Deal
ui.lunarSecret.line5: To the one who saved Earth!
ui.cine.intro.1: Earth has always been our home.
ui.cine.intro.2: We took poor care of it. Rivers shrank, forests faded and the sky changed.
ui.cine.intro.3: Cities began to run short of what they needed.
ui.cine.intro.4: So Project EARTH'S ANGEL was born: learning to live without wasting anything. Four crew members were chosen.
ui.cine.intro.5: Their ship, EL ANGEL, set out for the Moon.
ui.cine.intro.6: First mission: build a shelter where nothing runs out. Earth is counting the days.
ui.cine.moonToMars.1: The Moon base now runs on its own.
ui.cine.moonToMars.3: What they learned is already helping at home. Earth gains {bonus} days.
ui.cine.moonToMars.4: With that time, the Angel sets out for Mars.
ui.cine.moonToMars.5: Commander: This is El Ángel. All four of us have reached Mars.
ui.cine.moonToMars.6: Engineering: Look to the right! Another ship is landing.
ui.cine.moonToMars.7: Geology: We're the backup team. I can locate ice and other resources.
ui.cine.moonToMars.8: Communications: We're here to help! I'll keep us in touch with Earth.
ui.cine.moonToMars.9: Commander: Welcome! There are six of us now. Let's build this base together.
ui.cine.marsVictory.1: Commander: Oxygen, water, and food are stable.
ui.cine.marsVictory.earthFailed: We returned to Mars. Earth still needs help.
ui.cine.marsVictory.2: Engineering: The colony can sustain itself now.
ui.cine.marsVictory.3: Commander: Mars is self-sufficient! We did it, team!
ui.cine.marsVictory.4: Botany: Today's harvest is for everyone!
ui.cine.marsVictory.5: Communications: Earth, this is Mars. The colony is self-sufficient.
ui.cine.marsVictory.6: Earth Control: Copy that. We're already putting what you learned to work.
ui.cine.marsVictory.7: Commander: Today we celebrate what we built together.
ui.cine.marsVictory.8: Commander: And we gave Earth another chance.
ui.cine.wormhole.1: Both beacons wake at once. Something opens above the lab.
ui.cine.wormhole.3: The passage leads to Earth's past.
ui.cine.wormhole.4: Here, there is still time. Project Second Chance.
ui.cine.wormhole.banner: Time travel is part of the story, not real science.
ui.cine.earthVictory.1: What kept the base alive now cares for Earth.
ui.cine.earthVictory.4: The future begins by learning to care for our home. We still have time to protect Earth.
ui.manifest.heading: What travels to Mars
ui.manifest.arrivalNote: Half of the Moon supplies travel with you and are added to the Mars stockpile. Cargo power reads zero because the level starts with its own power.
ui.cards.title: Science cards
ui.learn.reviewPrompt: Now that the Moon mission is over, how would you prepare the base for a solar storm?
ui.result.lunarCheers: We did it, team! The base can sustain itself.
ui.cine.boarding.run: All aboard! Earth is counting on us.
ui.cine.boarding.rescue: Are you all right? Take my hand. We leave together.
ui.cine.boarding.launch: Crew aboard. Lifting off for Mars.
ui.walk.marsArrival: Explore Mars on foot. Q opens field actions and B opens the base. Build a self-sufficient colony and keep the link to Earth running. Dust can reduce solar power.
ui.hud.marsGravity: Mars gravity: 3.73 m/s², about 38% of Earth’s.
ui.practice.power.prompt: The solar panels are in shadow. Where can the base get power?
ui.practice.power.why: Solar panels need light to make electricity. A battery stores energy collected in sunlight and can power equipment while the panels are in shadow.
ui.practice.waterLoop.prompt: What can the Space Station use to recover water?
ui.practice.waterLoop.why: The system collects moisture from the air and treats used water. It tests the recovered water before returning it to the supply.
ui.practice.airFromWater.prompt: How can we get breathable oxygen from water?
ui.practice.airFromWater.B: By straining it through a mesh.
ui.practice.airFromWater.why: Electricity can split water into oxygen and hydrogen. This process is called electrolysis, and the International Space Station uses it.
ui.practice.solarStorm.prompt: A solar storm increases radiation. Where is the crew best protected?
ui.practice.solarStorm.B: In the most heavily shielded area.
ui.practice.solarStorm.why: The material around the shelter reduces the crew’s exposure to the particles. In the game, you also need to save enough power to use the shelter.
ui.learn.prompt: A solar storm reaches your Moon base tomorrow. What should you do first?
ui.learn.B: Have the shelter ready and save power to use it.
ui.learn.C: Turn every machine off to save power.
ui.learn.after: In your mission you saw that the shelter protects, and that using it has a cost.
ui.choice.heading: The colony is safe. What next?
ui.choice.stayBody: The colony is safe. A new chapter begins.
ui.choice.portalBody: The beacons open a path to Earth's past. One last mission.
ui.choice.portalWarning: If the Earth mission fails, you return to the Mars ending. You do not lose that victory.

ui.shelter.title: The crew is in the shelter
ui.shelter.body: Particles from the solar storm are passing outside. The thick shelter walls stop most of them, so the crew waits inside today.
ui.shelter.note: No building or exploring today. You can still end the day.
ui.presentation.start: Presentation mode: Earth's Angel plays itself. Press X at any time to stop.
ui.presentation.opening: Earth's Angel: design a space mission on Earth, launch it, and run it on the Moon and then on Mars.
ui.presentation.moon1: Day 1 on the Moon: two solar panels first. Without power, nothing else in the base works.
ui.presentation.moon2: Day 2: an ice extractor and a water recycler. Water is for drinking and for making oxygen.
ui.presentation.moon3: Day 3: the oxygen generator turns water into air, and the greenhouse grows food.
ui.presentation.moon4: Day 4: the panels are in shadow. A battery stores energy for the dark hours.
ui.presentation.moon5: Day 5: we build the radiation shelter before the solar storm arrives.
ui.presentation.moon6: Day 6: one more solar panel, so every system has power.
ui.presentation.moon7: Day 7: the base sustains itself. The forecast warns of a solar storm.
ui.presentation.moon8: Day 8: solar storm! The crew waits it out in the shielded shelter.
ui.presentation.moon9: Day 9: the storm has passed and the base is stable.
ui.presentation.moonStorm: A solar storm is coming: the commander decides whether the crew shelters.
ui.presentation.moonWin: The Moon base works on its own. Next stop: Mars.
ui.presentation.toMars: Half of the Moon supplies travel with the crew to Mars.
ui.presentation.marsArrive: Mars: a sol lasts about 24 h 40 min, dust covers the panels and radio messages to Earth take minutes. The small ship beside the base is the support ship.
ui.presentation.mars1: Sol 1: panels, oxygen generator and greenhouse at once. Mars starts with very little margin.
ui.presentation.mars2: Sol 2: ice extractors. There is frozen water on Mars that the colony can use.
ui.presentation.mars4: Sol 4: dust covers the panels, so the crew cleans them to get the power back.
ui.presentation.mars9: Sol 9: two shelters, so the whole crew of six fits during a solar storm.
ui.presentation.mars11: Sol 11: a communications antenna keeps the link with Earth.
ui.presentation.marsStorm: Solar storm on Mars: the crew goes into the shelter.
ui.presentation.marsWin: The Mars colony is self-sufficient. Mission accomplished!
ui.presentation.ending: Ending: the crew stays on Mars to keep the colony running.
ui.presentation.end: End of the presentation. Thank you! Press X to watch it again.

ui.presentation.loseStart: Defeat demo: what happens if the crew ignores life support? Press Z at any time to stop.
ui.presentation.lose1: Day 1: the crew only thinks about solar panels. Nobody plans water, air or food.
ui.presentation.lose2: Day 2: a battery and a mineral… but still no oxygen generator and no water.
ui.presentation.lose3: Day 3: more panels. Look at the warning over the astronaut: the reserves are falling.
ui.presentation.lose4: Day 4: the crew walks around the base without a plan.
ui.presentation.lose5: Day 5: only 2 days of oxygen left! The warning turns red, but nobody listens.
ui.presentation.lose6: Day 6: mission control insists. Still no oxygen generator and no water extractor.
ui.presentation.lose7: Day 7: the oxygen and the water have run out. The crew is in serious danger.
ui.presentation.loseStorm: A solar storm arrives, and the crew does not even go into the shelter.
ui.presentation.loseBoom: Life support failed. Without air, water and protection, the mission ends in disaster.

ui.trivia.title: Space question
ui.trivia.moonDistance.prompt: About how far is the Moon from Earth?
ui.trivia.moonDistance.why: On average the Moon is about 384,400 km away. About 30 Earths would fit in that gap.
ui.trivia.moonGravity.prompt: How strong is gravity on the Moon compared with Earth?
ui.trivia.moonGravity.why: Moon gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's, so a jump there goes about six times higher.
ui.trivia.marsGravity.prompt: How strong is gravity on Mars compared with Earth?
ui.trivia.marsGravity.why: Mars is smaller than Earth, so its gravity is only about 38% of ours.
ui.trivia.marsSol.prompt: How long is a day (a sol) on Mars?
ui.trivia.marsSol.why: A Mars solar day lasts about 24 hours and 40 minutes. Mission teams call it a sol.
ui.trivia.marsRed.why: Iron minerals in Martian rocks and dust have oxidized, or rusted, which gives Mars its red color.
ui.trivia.apollo11.prompt: Which mission first landed people on the Moon, in 1969?
ui.trivia.apollo11.why: On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon.
ui.trivia.moonWalkers.prompt: How many people have walked on the Moon?
ui.trivia.moonWalkers.why: Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon during the Apollo missions between 1969 and 1972.
ui.trivia.olympusMons.prompt: Where is the largest volcano in the solar system?
ui.trivia.olympusMons.why: Olympus Mons on Mars is about three times taller than Mount Everest.
ui.trivia.marsMoons.prompt: How many moons does Mars have?
ui.trivia.marsMoons.why: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.
ui.trivia.sunlightTime.prompt: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
ui.trivia.sunlightTime.why: Light from the Sun travels about 150 million km and reaches Earth in about 8 minutes.
ui.trivia.marsSignal.prompt: How long does a radio message take to go from Earth to Mars?
ui.trivia.marsSignal.why: It depends on where the planets are. That delay is why Mars rovers cannot be driven live like a toy car.
ui.trivia.issAltitude.prompt: About how high above Earth does the International Space Station fly?
ui.trivia.issAltitude.why: The station orbits about 400 km up, roughly the distance between two nearby cities.
ui.trivia.issOrbit.prompt: About how long does the Space Station take to go once around Earth?
ui.trivia.issOrbit.why: The station moves at about 28,000 km/h, so the crew sees about 16 sunrises a day.
ui.trivia.moonIce.prompt: Where is water ice found on the Moon?
ui.trivia.moonIce.right: In dark craters near the poles
ui.trivia.moonIce.why: Some craters near the lunar poles never get sunlight and are cold enough to keep water ice.
ui.trivia.moonAir.prompt: What is the air like on the Moon?
ui.trivia.moonAir.why: The Moon has only an extremely thin exosphere, so astronauts need spacesuits with their own oxygen.
ui.trivia.marsAir.prompt: What gas makes up most of the Martian atmosphere?
ui.trivia.marsAir.why: About 95% of Mars' thin atmosphere is carbon dioxide, so people cannot breathe it.
ui.trivia.moonFace.prompt: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon?
ui.trivia.moonFace.right: It spins once each time it orbits Earth
ui.trivia.moonFace.wrong1: It does not spin at all
ui.trivia.moonFace.why: The Moon is tidally locked: one turn on its axis takes as long as one orbit around Earth.
ui.trivia.moonDayLength.prompt: About how long is one full day (sunrise to sunrise) on the Moon?
ui.trivia.moonDayLength.why: A spot on the Moon gets about two weeks of sunlight and then about two weeks of night.
ui.trivia.perseverance.prompt: Which NASA rover landed in Jezero Crater on Mars in 2021?
ui.trivia.perseverance.why: Perseverance explores an ancient lake bed and collects rock samples that could be brought to Earth.
ui.trivia.ingenuity.prompt: What did the Ingenuity helicopter do first on Mars?
ui.trivia.ingenuity.right: The first powered flight on another planet
ui.trivia.ingenuity.why: In April 2021 Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
ui.trivia.curiosityPower.prompt: How does the Curiosity rover get its power?
ui.trivia.curiosityPower.right: From heat made by radioactive material
ui.trivia.curiosityPower.why: Curiosity uses a radioisotope power system, so it can work at night and through dusty seasons.
ui.trivia.opportunityEnd.prompt: What ended the Opportunity rover's mission in 2018?
ui.trivia.opportunityEnd.why: Dust blocked sunlight from its solar panels. Opportunity had worked for almost 15 years instead of 90 days.
ui.trivia.insightQuakes.prompt: What did NASA's InSight lander measure on Mars?
ui.trivia.insightQuakes.why: InSight's seismometer recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes and helped map the inside of Mars.
ui.trivia.insightDust.prompt: What made InSight's power drop until the mission ended in 2022?
ui.trivia.insightDust.why: Dust built up on its panels. In Earth's Angel, dust on Mars panels also lowers your power.
ui.trivia.artemis.prompt: What is the name of NASA's program to send astronauts back to the Moon?
ui.trivia.artemis.why: Artemis plans to land astronauts near the lunar south pole and learn to live there for longer.
ui.trivia.artemis1.prompt: What flew around the Moon on the Artemis I mission in 2022?
ui.trivia.artemis1.right: The Orion spacecraft, without a crew
ui.trivia.artemis1.why: Artemis I tested the SLS rocket and the Orion spacecraft on a flight around the Moon with no crew.
ui.trivia.sunStar.why: The Sun is a star, a huge ball of hot gas. It is the closest star to Earth.
ui.trivia.biggestPlanet.prompt: Which is the biggest planet in our solar system?
ui.trivia.biggestPlanet.why: Jupiter is so big that about 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.
ui.trivia.closestPlanet.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
ui.trivia.closestPlanet.why: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest one to the Sun.
ui.trivia.hottestPlanet.why: Venus' thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, so it is hotter than Mercury.
ui.trivia.solarWind.right: A stream of charged particles from the Sun
ui.trivia.solarWind.wrong1: Wind blowing on the Sun's surface
ui.trivia.solarWind.why: The Sun constantly sends out charged particles. Storms make the stream much stronger.
ui.trivia.aurora.prompt: What causes the northern and southern lights (auroras)?
ui.trivia.aurora.right: Particles from the Sun hitting our atmosphere
ui.trivia.aurora.why: Charged particles from the Sun are guided by Earth's magnetic field and make gases in the air glow.
ui.trivia.magneticShield.prompt: Why is radiation a bigger risk on the surface of Mars than on Earth?
ui.trivia.magneticShield.right: Mars has no global magnetic field and thin air
ui.trivia.magneticShield.wrong1: Mars is closer to the Sun
ui.trivia.magneticShield.why: Earth's magnetic field and thick air protect us. Mars lacks both, so crews need shielding.
ui.trivia.flareClass.prompt: Which letter marks the strongest class of solar flares?
ui.trivia.flareClass.why: Flares are ranked A, B, C, M and X. The storm in Earth's Angel comes from a real X8.2 flare in 2017.
ui.trivia.donki.prompt: What is NASA's DONKI used for?
ui.trivia.donki.right: Keeping records of space weather events
ui.trivia.donki.why: DONKI stores records of solar flares, storms and particle events. The game's storm comes from it.
ui.trivia.issWater.prompt: About how much of its water can the Space Station recover and reuse?
ui.trivia.issWater.wrong2: None, it is all brought from Earth
ui.trivia.issWater.why: In 2023 the station's life support reached about 98% water recovery, including water from sweat and urine.
ui.trivia.issFloat.prompt: Why do astronauts float inside the Space Station?
ui.trivia.issFloat.right: They are always falling around Earth
ui.trivia.issFloat.wrong1: There is no gravity up there
ui.trivia.issFloat.why: Gravity there is still about 90% of Earth's. The station and crew fall around Earth together, so they float.
ui.trivia.issLettuce.prompt: What did astronauts grow and eat on the Space Station in 2015?
ui.trivia.issLettuce.why: The Veggie experiment grew lettuce in space. Growing food will matter on long trips to Mars.
ui.trivia.moonOrigin.prompt: What is the leading idea about how the Moon formed?
ui.trivia.moonOrigin.right: A Mars-sized body hit the young Earth
ui.trivia.moonOrigin.why: Debris from a giant impact with the young Earth probably came together to form the Moon.
ui.trivia.regolith.prompt: What is the loose dust and rock on the Moon's surface called?
ui.trivia.regolith.why: Lunar regolith is sharp and sticky, and it could even be used to build shelters.
ui.trivia.footprints.prompt: Why can astronaut footprints last a very long time on the Moon?
ui.trivia.footprints.right: There is no wind or rain to erase them
ui.trivia.footprints.wrong1: The ground is made of glue
ui.trivia.footprints.why: With almost no air, there is no weather to wipe the marks away.
ui.trivia.moonTemperature.prompt: What are temperatures like on the Moon?
ui.trivia.moonTemperature.right: Very hot in sunlight and very cold at night
ui.trivia.moonTemperature.why: Without air to hold heat, the surface goes from above 120 °C in sunlight to below -130 °C at night.
ui.trivia.marsCold.prompt: What is the average temperature on Mars?
ui.trivia.marsCold.why: Mars is farther from the Sun and has thin air, so it is very cold on average.
ui.trivia.marsSize.prompt: How big is Mars compared with Earth?
ui.trivia.marsSize.why: Mars is about half the diameter of Earth.
ui.trivia.vallesMarineris.prompt: What is Valles Marineris on Mars?
ui.trivia.vallesMarineris.wrong2: A mountain range made of ice
ui.trivia.vallesMarineris.why: Valles Marineris is more than 4,000 km long, far bigger than the Grand Canyon.
ui.trivia.marsWater.prompt: What evidence shows Mars once had liquid water?
ui.trivia.marsWater.right: Old river valleys and lake beds
ui.trivia.marsWater.why: Rovers and orbiters found dry riverbeds, lake sediments and minerals that form in water.
ui.trivia.marsPoles.prompt: What are the polar caps of Mars made of?
ui.trivia.marsPoles.right: Water ice and frozen carbon dioxide
ui.trivia.marsPoles.why: The caps hold water ice, and in winter a layer of frozen carbon dioxide (dry ice) covers them.
ui.trivia.marsSunset.prompt: What color are sunsets on Mars?
ui.trivia.marsSunset.why: Fine Martian dust scatters blue light near the Sun, so sunsets there look blue.
ui.trivia.lightYear.why: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year: about 9.5 trillion km.
ui.trivia.closestStar.prompt: Which star is closest to our Sun?
ui.trivia.closestStar.why: Proxima Centauri is about 4.2 light-years away.
ui.trivia.milkyWay.prompt: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
ui.trivia.milkyWay.why: Our solar system is one of billions of star systems in the Milky Way galaxy.
ui.trivia.webb.prompt: Which space telescope launched in 2021 sees mainly in infrared light?
ui.trivia.webb.why: Webb sees infrared light, which lets it look at the first galaxies and through clouds of dust.
ui.trivia.voyager.prompt: Which spacecraft is the farthest human-made object from Earth?
ui.trivia.voyager.why: Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and entered interstellar space in 2012.
ui.trivia.moonOrbit.prompt: About how long does the Moon take to orbit Earth once?
ui.trivia.moonOrbit.why: The Moon goes around Earth about every 27.3 days.
ui.trivia.spacesuit.prompt: Why do astronauts need spacesuits outside?
ui.trivia.spacesuit.right: For air, pressure and protection from heat, cold and radiation
ui.trivia.spacesuit.wrong1: Only to look good in photos
ui.trivia.spacesuit.why: A spacesuit is a small personal spacecraft: it gives oxygen, keeps pressure and protects the body.
